title: Marlin Bay returns assistant field jot
summary: Raw capture from kickoff + technical intake with Marlin Bay (mid-size omnichannel retailer). Focus: lightweight Returns Assistant to speed RMA and reduce manual review. Notes include requirements, data gating, performance targets, likely gotchas and immediate next steps for a 6-week POC.
body:
Participants: Ava Chen (Redwood CS), Rajiv Kumar (Redwood Solutions), Sofia Martinez (Marlin Bay Head of Ops), Ethan Li (Marlin Bay SRE), Priya Nair (Marlin Bay Product).

Call context / goal:
- Intake / discovery: Marlin wants an assistant that can take a customer-initiated return request (web chat or email), classify reason, suggest return method, validate eligibility, and either auto-generate an RMA or route to ops for review. Primary goals: reduce manual review by 40%, speed to first response < 30s, and reduce refund slip errors.

Business constraints:
- Data sensitivity: orders contain PII (name, email, partial payment token). Marlin must keep all order/returns data in their VPC during POC. They prefer Redwood Private with customer-managed control plane or at minimum VPC peering for hosted API.
- Compliance: customer requested logs masked for card and SSN-like fields; audit trail needed for each assistant decision (who saw what, model version).
- Scale profile: peak returns season has spiky bursts - expected 150 reqs/min peak for POC traffic (10k/month). For production they estimate 2k reqs/min.

Technical / integration notes:
- Data sources: order DB (Postgres on AWS RDS), product catalog (S3 CSV + ElasticSearch), photo uploads (S3). They want to feed order metadata + last 3 messages + optional image of damaged item into the model.
- Preferred flow: client-side collects customer input + image, call Redwood inference endpoint with session token; Redwood routes to Marlin Bay private deployment.
- Authentication: Marlin uses Okta; they want JWT integration and short-lived model keys for service-to-service.
- Storage: session state should be ephemeral; persistent audit entries go to Marlin's audit DB only, Redwood retains minimal telemetry per signed agreement.

Model and behavior requirements:
- Primary behavior model: guided conversation with structured output (JSON fields: eligibility:true/false, reason_category, recommended_flow, rma_payload). They will validate structured output against schema in product.
- Confidence threshold: if model confidence < 0.7 OR image_analysis flags damage uncertain -> escalate to human queue.
- Image handling: use a separate image classifier (1st pass local heuristic) to detect obvious no-damage/damage; only attach image to main model call if damage detected or customer insists. Keep image bytes out of logs.

Performance SLOs / cost sensitivity:
- Latency targets: 95th <= 350ms for text-only requests, 95th <= 900ms when image analysis invoked.
- Cost: Marlin is cost-sensitive; aim for hosted-like per-call economics but they will accept Dedicated/GPU reserved for production if it meets SLOs. For POC they want evaluation on a smaller model variant and fall back to larger model only for complex escalations.

Gotchas / edge cases called out:
- Partial barcodes & SKU synonyms: catalog data is messy; fuzzy matching required. If match uncertain, assistant must ask one clarifying question rather than guessing.
- Returns windows: some items have time-limited return windows by country; need to surface rule and the evidence (order date).
- Fraud signals: high-value returns with mismatched shipping address should trigger human review. Marlin wants a simple risk score in the structured output.
- Multi-item returns in one conversation: customers often combine items - the assistant must enumerate items clearly and allow per-item decisions.
- International labels: different carriers and pre-paid label generation flows per region.

Proposed Redwood config & architecture for POC:
- Deployment: Redwood Private (VPC) with a small dedicated pool (2x small GPUs) for the POC. Use routing policy to prefer quantized medium model for typical requests, fallback to larger generative model for escalations.
- Caching & batching: enable prefix / KV cache for repeated return templates (common phrases) to shave latency. Use short batching window (10ms) during bursts.
- Observability: per-route token and latency breakdown in Redwood Console; enable trace hooks to link requests to Marlin's audit IDs.
- Rollout plan: canary with 5% of production traffic after POC, A/B test with baseline human workflow for accuracy comparisons.

POC scope (6 weeks suggested):
- Week 0: infra prep, sign NDA + security questionnaire, network brokering for VPC.
- Week 1: ingest product catalog sample + order sample, mapping of SKU fields, basic fuzzy match rules.
- Week 2: build minimal UI wiring (chat widget) + image upload toggle, hooking to Redwood Private endpoint.
- Week 3: baseline model behavior tuning (prompt templates, extraction schema), initial evaluation set creation.
- Week 4: human-in-the-loop queue integration, escalation path, audit log validation.
- Week 5: load testing for 150 reqs/min bursts, latency tuning (batching, kernel selection).
- Week 6: final demo, handoff doc, and SLO/contract discussion.

Immediate action items / owners:
- Ava: send security questionnaire + sample contract redlines to Marlin (due EOD 2025-02-21).
- Rajiv: spin up Private cluster spec and cost estimate for 6-week POC (due 2025-02-24).
- Sofia: provide sanitized sample of 500 orders, product catalog subset, and 50 representative images (due 2025-02-25).
- Ethan: confirm Okta JWT flow details and provide SRE contact for VPC peering (due 2025-02-21).
- Priya: share acceptance criteria for automated RMAs (what counts as "auto-approved") and sample rule exceptions (due 2025-02-23).

Notes to self / brainstorm snippets:
- Consider embedding-based SKU resolver: create a small vector index of catalog titles + synonyms to improve fuzzy SKU matching. Put nearest-neighbor match score in structured output.
- For images, prototype a small MobileNet-style classifier hosted in Marlin infra (Lambda) to return "damage_confident" flag before calling main model to avoid token/image cost.
- Keep escrowed model logs: store only hashed IDs for audit traceability to satisfy Marlin privacy.
- Hook Redwood Optimize to surface batching/quantization recommendations after Week 3 load test.

Risks flagged:
- If Marlin insists on full on-prem air-gapped, POC timeline slips (additional infra work + security review).
- Catalog quality may dominate false positives for auto-approvals; need conservative thresholds early.

Open questions to clarify on next call:
- Does Marlin require explicit human-readable explanation for each decision (e.g., "because order date is > 30 days") or is an internal audit trail sufficient?
- Are there any third-party returns vendors (label generation) we must integrate with during POC or will Marlin provide an API stub?
- How long must Redwood retain telemetry (they suggested 30 days but legal may want different term)?

Next meeting suggested: 2025-02-24 10:00 PT — technical kickoff with SRE + Okta + sample dataset handoff.

Quick checklist for the kickoff:
- NDA + security questionnaire complete
- Sample data sanitized and uploaded to shared S3 bucket
- Okta config + JWT flow tested with staging client
- Redwood Private cluster spec shared and cost-approved

Rough acceptance criteria for POC success (for CS to measure):
- 40% reduction in human-reviewed RMAs on covered categories
- 95th percentile latency meets targets for 80% of traffic during simulated bursts
- Structured output precision for eligibility >= 88% on evaluation set
- Clear rollback path to human-only routing if accuracy dips below threshold

Misc small notes:
- Marlin uses a weird SKU format "MB-XXXX-YYYY" and sometimes omits prefix in refunds; strip/normalize during ETL.
- They asked for a short FAQ snippet for ops staff: "When to escalate" and "How to validate image evidence" — draft separately.

End of raw capture. Will tidy into a short pilot brief and share with Marlin later this week.
